It is the aorist infinitive, written γηρᾶναι [to grow old] almost constantly in the manuscripts of writers, whose participle is γηράς [having grown old]. I have spoken about these forms in the Thesaurus vol. 2 p. 609. There is one example in Aeschylus.
Which is said by tmesis for συγγηράναι [to grow old together]. For Auratus rightly restored σύν [with] for vûv.
